record.what_it_does: Discord's API lets developers build bots and apps that send/receive messages, manage servers (guilds), channels, members, roles, and interactions on behalf of users or as automated bot accounts.
record.auth_notes: Bots authenticate with a static bot token (issued per-application in the Developer Portal, format `Authorization: Bot TOKEN`), which functions like a Bearer/API key for the app's own actions. User-scoped actions (acting on behalf of an end user, e.g. reading their guild list) use standard OAuth2 authorization code grant with access/refresh tokens. A special 'bot authorization flow' (scope=bot) lets a user install a bot to a server without a full OAuth redirect.
record.access_notes: Anyone can create a Developer Portal account and application for free, generate a bot token, and start calling the API/gateway immediately, and install the bot in up to 100 servers with no review. Scaling a bot past 100 servers requires 'App Verification' (team identity verification via Stripe), and privileged gateway intents (e.g. message content) now require review once an app crosses a 10,000-user threshold — so production/multi-tenant use hits approval_required-like gates even though initial dev access is free and instant.
record.main_blocker: App verification (Stripe identity check) required to scale a bot beyond 100 servers, and privileged intent review needed for message-content access at scale
